title: WHO Clinical Management of Acute Coronary Syndromes and Chest Pain
snippet: Patients presenting with acute substernal chest pressure, pain radiating to the left arm or jaw, or severe acute dyspnea require immediate emergency evaluation to rule out acute myocardial infarction.

title: NHS Clinical Guidelines: Stroke, TIA, and Migraine Triage
snippet: Sudden unilateral numbness, facial drooping, or speech difficulty (FAST criteria) mandates emergency stroke pathway activation. Recurrent throbbing unilateral headaches without focal neurological deficits should be referred to a neurologist.

title: NHS Guidance on Acute Otitis Media, Tinnitus, and Pharyngitis
snippet: Persistent earache accompanied by tinnitus, muffled hearing, or severe sore throat without airway compromise warrants evaluation by an Ear, Nose, and Throat (ENT) specialist.

title: Mayo Clinic: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) and Acute GI Bleeding
snippet: Epigastric burning, heartburn after meals, and non-bloody diarrhea are managed by a gastroenterologist or internist. Hematemesis (vomiting blood) or melena requires immediate emergency intervention.

title: Mayo Clinic: Sciatica, Lower Back Pain, and Joint Disorders
snippet: Lower back pain radiating down the leg (sciatica) or chronic knee joint stiffness without acute bowel/bladder incontinence should be evaluated by an orthopedic and spine specialist.

title: WHO Primary Care Triage for Fever and Dermatological Eruptions
snippet: Low-to-moderate grade fever with generalized fatigue or localized pruritic skin rash without mucosal swelling should be assessed by an internal medicine or dermatology specialist.
